title: DTCR candidate review card
description: The reader-facing half of a synthesis: what was claimed against what was observed, over which subject, at which coverage ceiling, with which invariants violated, which retrieved context was consulted and how stale it was, what the change would buy and cost, how it could fail, what is still unknown, which negative controls have to run, what is recommended, who owns the lease, how it would be verified, and what is not proven. The card is a recommendation. Its class is pinned MODEL_SUMMARY_RECOMMENDATION and its decision fields are pinned empty with the state HUMAN_ADMIT_REQUIRED, because MODEL_SUMMARY != REVIEW_DECISION and a summary that arrives with the decision already written in it is not reviewed, it is ratified. The seven hard laws are carried as a required object of false constants rather than as prose, so a card that promotes one of them fails a schema check instead of reading persuasively.

card_class.description: Fixed. The card is a model summary of compiled facts; it is never the review decision, and the two are told apart here rather than by the tone of the prose.

subject_commit.description: Exact commit. A branch, a tag, main or latest names a moving tree and dates the packet to nothing.

claim_source_ref.description: Where the claim came from. A claim with no source is one the card invented while summarising.

measurement_class.description: A static count over the tree and an executed measurement of the running system are different observations. There is no value here meaning benchmark, because a benchmark is a run and this vocabulary describes what a compiler read.

benchmark_established.description: STATIC_METRIC != BENCHMARK, pinned. Nothing a fact plane produces establishes a throughput or latency result, so no row of this card may say one was established.

analysed.description: The literal NOT_MEASURED or a numerator over a named denominator. No key here holds a percentage.

unanalysed_inputs_cleared.description: What was not analysed was not cleared. Carried onto the card because the ceiling is the field a summary drops first.

behavior_preserved.description: NO_ILLEGAL_GRAPH_EDGE != BEHAVIOR_PRESERVED, pinned. A graph query that finds no forbidden edge has looked at the edges it resolved; behaviour is preserved by a run, not by a query.

then.description: A heuristic edge set is a lower bound, on the card for the same reason it is a lower bound on the violation candidate it came from.

statement.description: Written out. A rule referred to only by identifier is a rule nobody can disagree with.

unresolved_case_refs.description: Cases that are open or blocked rather than confirmed. Folding them into the violated list turns a nomination into a finding; dropping them turns an unexamined case into a clean one.

back_reference_ref.description: The exact source behind the row. A card that cites context without one asks the reader to trust a rank.

basis_grade.description: The same constant the consumed context row and the violation candidate carry, so a row keeps its ceiling when it reaches the card.

influence.description: A retrieved row may explain why a finding matters and may never be why it exists.

establishes_current_failure.description: RETRIEVED_INCIDENT != CURRENT_FAILURE, pinned. An incident write-up is evidence that something once happened somewhere, never that it is happening in this subject now.

then.description: An inapplicable lane with rows in it was applicable.

grade.description: ANALYST_EXPECTATION where no deterministic observation is named. An expectation printed beside an observed fact in the same list becomes one by proximity.
ANALYST_EXPECTATION where no deterministic observation is named. An expectation printed beside an observed fact in the same list becomes one by proximity.
ANALYST_EXPECTATION where no deterministic observation is named. An expectation printed beside an observed fact in the same list becomes one by proximity.

resolved_by.description: The thing somebody would run to stop it being unknown. An unknown with no route out of it is a disclaimer.

required_negative_controls.description: At least one. A review that lists only what would confirm it has no way of being wrong, and a check that cannot go red is not a check.

action.description: Three values, and deliberately no value meaning merge, approve or ship. Those are operations a person performs.

binding.description: Fixed. The mutation this refuses is a reviewer recommendation travelling one hop and arriving as an automatic merge.

task_state_writer_count.description: One mutable task state has one writer. A second writer makes the ledger a record of whoever ran last, and the card that named two of them cannot be reconstructed afterwards.

arrival.description: STATIC proves a thing is possible, SANDBOX that it executes under synthetic input, PROD that it ran with these values. None of the three implies either other.

denominator_definition.description: What the step counts over, written out. Without it the ratio describes a set the reader invents, and the set the reader invents is always the whole system.

negative_denominator.description: ONE_GREEN_TEST != FULL_DENOMINATOR. A step with no case that would go red measures whether the harness runs.

executed.description: A plan is not a run. Compiling an oracle never sets this, and a receipt from the lane that ran it is a separate artifact.

claims_not_proven.description: TECHNICAL_PASS != USER_OR_PAID_VALIDATION. Every card states that user value is unproven, whatever its technical lanes reported, because the sentence a passing card suppresses first is the one about the people it was for.

decision_text.description: Pinned empty by the compiler on every card regardless of input. The decision is Human/Tech-Lead owned and is recorded elsewhere by whoever made it.

hard_laws.description: Seven promotions, each named after the thing it would be promoted into, each pinned false and all seven required. A card that drops one has stopped carrying the law rather than broken it, which is why the required list is closed.

allOf.description: And the paid lane, separately: a repository can pass every technical check it owns without one person having paid for the result.
